processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Fe-16%Al monocrystals up to 10 cm length grown by the Bridgman method with 10–15 mm/h pulling rate; crystal growth with subsequent cooling occurred within a time period of about 12 h.

processing_steps.method: etching in ammonium persulfate ((NH4)2S2O8) and orientation by a laser light-figure method
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Monocrystals were etched and oriented after growth; the as-grown state is used without any further heat treatment.

processing_steps.method: electrostatic discharge machining, grinding and diamond-paste polishing
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Compression specimens with dimensions 5×5×10 mm³ had their surfaces cleansed by grinding and the monocrystals were polished with 3 µm diamond paste before testing (monocrystals were not cleansed by ultrasound in acetone).

structures.overall_structure: Monocrystalline (single-crystal) Fe-16%Al; body-centred cubic Fe-Al solid solution; the hardness specimens are (111) oriented and the compression specimens are [112] oriented; contains rare globular AlN inclusions; no carbides present because no heat treatment was applied (as-grown).

inclusions: rare globular AlN inclusions with diameters up to 30 µm (identified by EDX)

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: (111)-oriented Fe-16%Al monocrystal in the as-grown state; universal hardness HU measured with a Fischerscope H100 (max load 1 N), HU = F/(26.43·h²)
[112]-oriented Fe-16%Al monocrystal in the as-grown state; compressive loading

stress_strain_curves.value: compressive stress-strain curve at RT and 10^-4 s^-1: steep rise to a knee at ~1.5–2% strain, then a nearly flat plateau near 430–440 MPa up to ~5.5% strain

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Fischerscope H100 microhardness tester (maximum load 1 N); HU = F/(26.43·h²) [N/mm²]; reported HU values are averages of more than 40 measurements
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Room temperature; (111)-oriented Fe-16%Al monocrystal, as-grown and variously heat-treated
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine the effect of prior heat treatment / state of atomic order on the hardness of the Fe-16%Al monocrystal
characterization_methods.key_findings: As-grown monocrystal HU ≈2000 N/mm²; heat treatment shifts HU by only about 5–10%

characterization_methods.technique: Compressive testing (yield stress determined as 0.2% proof stress)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Room temperature and -100°C; strain rates 10^-4 s^-1 and 10^-2 s^-1
characterization_methods.purpose: Study the stress-strain behaviour of the Fe-16%Al monocrystal as a function of prior heat treatment
characterization_methods.key_findings: [112]-oriented as-grown Fe-16%Al monocrystal shows a knee at ~1.5–2% strain and a nearly flat plateau near 430–440 MPa at room temperature and 10^-4 s^-1

characterization_methods.technique: Optical microscopy and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) with energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) analysis
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Optical microscope; SEM with EDX; specimens etched in alcoholic 10% nitric acid

characterization_methods.key_findings: Monocrystals contain rare globular AlN inclusions with diameters up to 30 µm (identified by EDX); no carbides detected in as-grown monocrystals

characterization_methods.key_findings: Fe-16%Al monocrystal real composition: Al 16.0 at.% (8.4 wt.-%), impurities C 45, Si 40, O 60 wt.ppm

unmapped_findings: Fe-16%Al monocrystal (Table 1) real composition: Al 16.0 at.% (8.4 wt.-%), impurities C 45, Si 40, O 60 wt.ppm.
The monocrystals contained rare globular AlN inclusions with diameters up to 30 µm, identified by EDX analysis.
No carbides were detected in the Fe-16%Al monocrystal with 45 ppm C after a heat treatment of 14 days at 320°C; without heat treatment no carbides were found in all monocrystals.

In the hardness study (Fig. 1) the as-grown Fe-16%Al monocrystal hardness equals that measured after a 250°C/14 day anneal (maximum ordering), quench from 600°C, furnace cooling from 1100°C to RT, and 300°C/6h and 300°C/3d anneals; lower hardness resulted from 300°C/14d and higher-temperature anneals, and higher hardness from quenching from 1100°C (with and without subsequent anneal).
Short-range ordering was concluded to have no major impact on hardness; only heat treatments at temperatures above 600°C affect the mechanical behaviour of Fe-Al alloys significantly.

The as-grown monocrystal stress-strain curve differs only little from the furnace-cooled and 1100°C FC 600°C Q states, whereas quenching from 1100°C with subsequent 300°C/14d anneal gives a higher yield stress.
